items: Misr Insurance Holding will sell 15% of Misr Life Insurance on the EGX in December, with EFG Hermes as sole bookrunner → the IMF wants about $1.5 bn of asset sales before the programme ends; Banque du Caire has delivered $658 mn so far.
EGX30 falls 0.99% to 51,682 on Tuesday and the EGX70 drops another 2.42% → local investors are the sole net sellers as small caps extend their slide.
Gold drops below $3,800 as Fed officials signal more rate hikes; 21K gold in Egypt slips to EGP 5,900 → higher US yields and a firm dollar weigh on bullion and on emerging-market carry.
The Arab Energy Fund files a $70 mn tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive at $0.70 a share → Gulf money keeps buying into EGX-listed energy services.

Seven fertiliser makers agree to pay 50% more for gas, $12.75 per mmBtu and $175 mn upfront, in return for exporting their full output until early January → the state recovers some LNG costs while producers keep selling urea at about $535 a tonne; gas cuts of 20-40% stay.
EGX30 ends flat at 52,200 on Monday but the EGX70 drops 3.76% and the EGX100 2.88% → small caps sell off while Edita (+7.4%) and Telecom Egypt (+5.2%) hold up the blue-chip index.
Edita posts record quarterly revenue of EGP 7.3 bn, up 32.9%, with profit up 41.5% → volume growth and pricing lift the snack maker, and the stock jumps 7.44%.
Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd move three more Gemini services back to the Suez Canal from December → more Asia-Europe traffic adds to canal revenue and dollar inflows.

Egypt raises the private-sector minimum wage 21% to EGP 8,500 a month from 1 January 2027, covering about 26.5 mn workers → higher wages lift consumer spending but raise costs for labour-heavy industries.
TMG Holding's nine-month profit rises 11.9% to EGP 11.72 bn, Fawry's 32% and Edita's 54% → earnings season keeps delivering growth for EGX blue chips.
ONE's container ship crosses the Suez Canal and three more Premier Alliance services are set to follow → the return of Asian carriers adds to canal revenue and dollar inflows.
EGX30 rises 0.31% to 52,187 on Sunday, led by Orascom Construction (+3.4%) and AMOC (+4.8%) → the index is up 24.8% this year, though turnover runs 17% below its 90-day average.

Egypt's final IMF review moves to virtual talks with about $2.3 bn at stake before the programme ends on 15 December → the Cairo mission ended without a staff-level deal; a miss would delay funds and could unsettle the pound.
Telecom Egypt's nine-month profit jumps 43.7% to EGP 24.38 bn and Elsewedy Electric's rises 20.7% to EGP 15.30 bn → two large listed companies report strong growth ahead of Sunday's session.

An ENGIE-led group with Orascom Construction closes $588 mn of debt for a 900 MW wind farm at Ras Shokeir → the project doubles the group's wind capacity in Egypt and gives Orascom a construction contract.
Iran says it targets a US base in Bahrain again as Saudi forces down Houthi drones; Brent ends the week at $96.13 → Gulf attacks keep oil high and Egypt's energy bill under pressure.

Trump says the US no longer needs a deal with Iran and tells Vance to drop the talks, while the blockade stays → the end of diplomacy keeps Gulf energy at risk; oil ends the week at $96.13 and European gas jumps 12%.
European gas surges 12% in a week to €96.18/MWh, and Goldman sees €150 in early 2027 if Gulf LNG stays disrupted → costlier LNG raises Egypt's energy import bill and costs for gas-heavy industry.
Gold has its worst week since March, down 4.7%, and 21K gold in Egypt falls 2.7% to EGP 5,950 a gram → markets see a December Fed hike as certain, which lifts the dollar.
EGX30 ends the week at 52,023, up about 1.7% (derived), led by banks → QNB Egypt rises four sessions in a row and Housing and Development Bank jumps 5.79% on Thursday.

key.l: IMF funds agreed at staff level

stories.h: IMF reaches staff-level agreement on Egypt's final reviews, worth $2.3 bn
stories.what: IMF staff led by Amine Mati agree with Egypt on the eighth and final review of the $8 bn Extended Fund Facility (about $1.5 bn) and the third review of the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (up to $0.8 bn), pending board approval before the facility expires on 15 December. The IMF backs the CBE's October hike, sets a 7% inflation target for Q4 2027 and wants faster asset sales, timely fuel price changes and a smaller state role. "Exchange-rate flexibility should remain the first line of defense," it says.
stories.why: The IMF welcomes the Banque du Caire IPO, and Egypt aims to cut gross financing needs by 5% of GDP this fiscal year.
stories.aff: The pound, reserves, Egypt's credit outlook and the state's divestment pipeline.
stories.eg: Total IMF disbursements would reach about $9.6 bn, closing the programme on time.
stories.egx: Bullish for banks and foreign-held blue chips; more state IPOs ahead.

key.l: real GDP growth, July to September 2026

stories.h: Growth picks up to 4.9% as unemployment rises to 6%
stories.what: Egypt's economy grows 4.9% year on year in the first quarter of FY2026/27, up from 4.7% in the previous quarter but below 5.3% a year earlier. Unemployment rises to 6.0% from a record low of 5.8%.
stories.why: EnterpriseAM gives no breakdown of the drivers.
stories.aff: Corporate earnings, consumer demand and the labour market.
stories.eg: Steady growth supports earnings, while higher joblessness may soften spending.

stories.h: Orascom Construction's profit nearly doubles; EFG Holding's Q3 profit falls 15%
stories.what: Orascom Construction's nine-month net profit rises 95.9% to $218 mn on revenue up 39.5% to $4.78 bn; new awards rise 90.4% to $7.08 bn and the backlog reaches $11.61 bn. EnterpriseAM puts its Q3 net income up 103% to $102.7 mn. EFG Holding's Q3 revenue rises 5% to EGP 6.7 bn while net income falls 15% to EGP 720 mn. Orascom rises 0.85% and EFG Holding 5.02% on Wednesday.
stories.why: Orascom's new awards rise 90%; EnterpriseAM gives no reason for EFG's profit fall.
stories.eg: Orascom's merger shares list on 24 November.
stories.egx: Bullish for Orascom Construction; mixed for EFG Holding.

stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Arab Finance; EnterpriseAM
stories.what: The EGX30 falls 0.26% to 51,544.82 on Wednesday and the EGX70 0.16%; market cap is EGP 4.08 tn. Turnover drops to EGP 6.67 bn, 40.3% below the 90-day average. Arabs net buy EGP 174 mn while Egyptians and foreigners sell. EFG Holding (+5.02%) gains, while Emaar Misr (-2.19%) and Edita (-2.16%) fall. The CBE quotes 53.89 per dollar.
stories.why: The sources give no single cause; the index is still up 23.2% this year.
stories.names: EFG Holding (up); Emaar Misr, Edita, Elsewedy (down).

key.l: spot gold's fall on Wednesday 18 Nov

stories.h: Gold falls 3.2% to a 14-month low as Fed minutes point to more hikes
stories.what: Spot gold falls 3.2% on Wednesday to its lowest close since September 2025, then rises 0.8% to $3,754.85 on Thursday morning. Minutes of the Fed's October meeting show almost all officials expect more hikes, and Governor Waller urges considering 50 basis points in December. In Egypt, Banky puts 21K gold at EGP 5,750 a gram, down 0.95%.
stories.why: Higher US rates and a firm dollar weigh on gold.

stories.h: Oil steadies near $92 as Hormuz flows return to pre-war levels
stories.what: Brent is at $92.00 on Thursday morning after falling 1.3% on Wednesday, while WTI hits its lowest since 26 August. Crude shipments through Hormuz are back near pre-war levels and US stocks rise 3.4 mn barrels, but Iran says three tankers are disabled by mines. "Oil is caught between bearish fundamentals and bullish geopolitical risks," says Phillip Nova's Priyanka Sachdeva.
stories.eg: Brent near $92 eases Egypt's energy costs.
